findings.text: the receipt records revision 9c4a2257aba7 (the solve commit) and _render_receipt copies it into render-receipt.json, but the three committed PNGs were drawn at c0dfe1f00, which is the commit that adds the media-painter drawing code and regenerates them; a reader who resolves the receipt's revision against the tree therefore finds the figures drawn by a later revision than the one stamped, so the stamp names the solve rather than the drawing code. Minor: the diagnostic numbers come from the solve and do not depend on the painters, so the staleness is a labelling gap, not a wrong measurement.

test_panels_are_titled_for_the_state_each_one_shows validates each PNG only by existence and size>5000 and compares the title by re-deriving it through the same census_title() the driver used to write it, so the guard cannot fail on a re-render that keeps the receipt but omits the first wall, the EFIT axis or the admission verdict from the panel, nor on a PNG that no longer matches its render-receipt entry. The independent render-only byte-identity check I ran (sha256 match for all three PNGs and the render-receipt) closes the stale-PNG case here, but it is not part of the guard.

follow_ons: Outside this node's write scope and not blocking it: (1) the receipt's revision field names the solve revision (9c4a2257a) rather than the revision the panels were drawn at, so a reader cannot tell the drawing code revision from the receipt alone; (2) the guard validates the PNG only by existence and size, so it would not catch a re-render that omitted the first wall or the admission verdict — closing that belongs in the test, not this node's artifacts.
